title: Baby Comfort Guide Insight - User Evaluation Study
summary:
Excessive crying, sleeping, and feeding problems are among the most common mental health concerns in infancy and early childhood, affecting approximately 10–30% of infants and young children. These difficulties are often associated with an impaired ability of the child to self-regulate and can place a considerable burden on affected families. Parents frequently report feeling exhausted, helpless, and uncertain, particularly when the problems persist despite repeated attempts to soothe and care for their child. Persistent regulatory problems may also negatively affect the parent–child relationship and are associated with an increased risk of later emotional and behavioral difficulties in the child. Early access to evidence-based support is therefore of great importance. However, many parents delay seeking professional help or do not seek it at all, for example due to fear of stigmatization or because appropriate support services are not easily accessible.

Digital health interventions can provide parents with an accessible and low-threshold source of support. For this purpose, the Baby Comfort Guide app (formerly Unser kleiner Schreihals; DRKS00019001) was developed. The app provides evidence-based information on crying, sleeping, and feeding problems and offers practical guidance for managing these challenges in everyday life. A randomized controlled trial demonstrated that using the app reduced parental stress and improved parents' knowledge of crying, sleeping, and feeding problems. In addition, participating parents rated the app as helpful and user-friendly. Based on these findings, the app was further refined and subsequently released free of charge.

To establish the app as an effective long-term preventive support tool and to continuously adapt it to the needs of families, the current project aims to evaluate how the app is used and perceived in routine practice. To this end, anonymized in-app usage data (e.g., frequency and duration of use) will be analyzed. In addition, users will complete a questionnaire assessing the app's usefulness, usability, and the different content and features it provides. The findings will be used to further optimize the app and ensure that it continues to meet the needs of families.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All adult participants who voluntarily provide their consent to the analysis of anonymized usage data and/or voluntarily participate in the anonymous questionnaire and are able to understand the study instructions are included.
Exclusion criteria:
Individuals who do not provide consent to participate in the study and/or to the collection of anonymized data are excluded.
